chunks: And Ya'qub ibn Yazid narrated from Yahya ibn al-Mubarik from Abdullah ibn Jabala from Abu Jamilyah from Isma'il ibn 'Ammar from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)
In the case of parents and a maternal grandmother, he said: 'For the mother is one-sixth, and for the maternal grandmother is one-sixth, and what remains, which is two-thirds, is for the father.'
ai.seo_question: What is the share of the maternal grandmother in Islamic inheritance when the father and mother are also alive?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the specific shares of the mother, maternal grandmother, and father in the presence of other heirs, establishing a cumulative distribution where each receives one-sixth. It highlights the Shia jurisprudential principle that the maternal grandmother is a distinct heir alongside the mother, with the father receiving the residual two-thirds as a 'sahib al-farid' (holder of the fixed share). This ruling is foundational in the chapter of 'Mirath man 'ala' (inheritance of ascendants) within al-Tusi's Tahdhib al-Ahkam.
